title: Integrated online opponent-seat gradient contract smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The ordinary integrated PPO plus legacy replay update exhibits measurable online opponent-seat conflict at the 1M Seed1 checkpoint, and identity coverage becomes complete as two legacy replay generations are replaced without resetting optimizer, hand counters, pool, assignment RNG, or replay semantics.
material_change: Add an opt-in non-mutating online gradient probe that records opponent identity in new transitions, treats pre-feature replay identities as explicit legacy unknowns, forms supported opponent-seat PPO and Standard10 source-KL objectives from known rows, and measures their alignment with the actual full actor update; continue Seed1 for only a four-iteration mechanism smoke.
baseline: Frozen Seed1 1M integrated checkpoint: 1,049,269 actual environment hands; prior offline audit found material opponent-seat conflicts and ordinary aggregate harm, while seven-objective one-shot updates had mixed fresh breadth.

notes: This is a contract/mechanism smoke, not a Slumbot or route-rejection gate. Legacy serialized replay tuples predate opponent identity; they remain in the actual update and are explicitly counted unknown for diagnostics until normal two-generation eviction replaces them. No optimizer, counter, replay, pool, or assignment reset is permitted.

Resume staging passed all nine gates: source iteration220/1,049,269 actual hands, optimizer/replay/dynamic-pool/adaptive-league/assignment chain serialized, and new fixed-deal start 20,100,000 exceeds first-unused upper bound 16,168,500.

Training stopped naturally at the first PPO boundary beyond the preregistered target: iteration224, 1,068,985 cumulative actual environment hands, 19,716 new environment hands and 16,397 new policy transitions. The 22-gate continuation audit passed; optimizer, replay, pool, assignment chain, bridge, trust region and accounting remained continuous.

Mean known-identity coverage progressed 0.6667, 0.8307, 1.0, 1.0 as the two legacy replay generations were normally evicted. No replay entries were discarded or rewritten. All eight probes had at least one objective opposed by the actual aggregate actor update; all four full-coverage probes harmed 4-5 of 11 supported objectives. Standard10 source-KL alignment was positive in 8/8, so the conflict is among reward opponent-seat groups rather than source preservation.

result.summary: A four-iteration exact-state continuation added 19,716 actual environment hands and reached full replay identity coverage without any reset. All continuation gates and 322 tests passed. Every one of eight online probes found the ordinary full actor update harmful to at least one supported objective; at full coverage it harmed 4-5 of 11 objectives per probe, while source-KL alignment stayed positive throughout.
result.conclusion: The earlier frozen offline conflict finding translates to the actual replay-bearing online optimizer path. Legacy replay metadata is not a blocker: explicit unknown accounting converged monotonically to full coverage after normal two-generation eviction. This is replicated mechanism evidence for trying conflict-aware online aggregation, not evidence that the long-horizon integrated family fails and not a Slumbot claim.
result.next_step: Implement an opt-in all-policy-heads-only online MGDA/common-descent actor aggregation that preserves the ordinary critic update and exact replay/accounting semantics. First verify bitwise control equivalence when disabled and positive alignment plus bounded update scale in a very short matched mechanism smoke; only then evaluate fresh multi-anchor breadth and decide geometric scaling.
